footnotes: Banks have no cost of sales; the flow chart shows revenue (net interest income + noninterest income) going to noninterest expense and the provision for credit losses, leaving pre-tax income. Other items, net are the gains and charges the income statement shows outside these lines (−$1.9M in 2025). From pre-tax income to net loss: includes a $50.7M income tax benefit. Efficiency ratio = noninterest expense ÷ revenue (lower is better).
Figures are from the company's Form 10-K for fiscal years ended Dec 31, 2025 and a year earlier, as filed with the SEC. Never estimated: items the filing does not report are left out.
Percentages are of revenue; figures may not sum due to rounding.

summary: Revenue (net interest income plus noninterest income) changed to −$27.0M in 2025. Net interest income rose 21.7% to $229M and noninterest income was −$256M, versus $3.0M; noninterest expense rose 8.5%, and the provision for credit losses was $0, versus $0.
Net loss was −$150M, versus $35.4M, or −$3.24 per diluted share, and the efficiency ratio was -638.9% versus 82.9%. Horizon Bancorp returned $29.5M through dividends.
sources: Horizon Bancorp, Inc. Form 10-K for FY2025 (SEC EDGAR)
